pr.title: Move `cmp_in_dominator_order` out of graph dominator computation
pr.description:
Dominator-order information is only needed for coverage graphs, and is easy enough to collect by just traversing the graph again.

This avoids wasted work when computing graph dominators for any other purpose.
pr.author: Zalathar

processing.reason: The PR is a performance-only refactor and does not contain a historically incorrect semantic transformation. Before the PR, `domin when_impl` recorded each reachable node's DFS postorder rank, and `cmp_in_dominator_order` compared `post_order_rank[rhs].cmp(&post_order_rank[lhs])`. After the PR, `CoverageGraph` obtains the same DFS postorder via `graph::iterate::reverse_post_order`, reverses it, and assigns ascending ranks, then compares `rank[a].cmp(&rank[b])`. These are the same total ordering for every reachable coverage-graph node, and the PR explicitly asserts that all coverage-graph nodes are reachable. The old `Kind::Path` index ordering and the new reverse-postorder ordering also agree on path-shaped coverage graphs. Therefore any source-grounded pair would produce identical values for original and transformed functions; claiming a semantic counterexample would require inventing a different, unjustified bug such as failing to initialize the new rank table or comparing unreachable nodes, which the PR excludes by construction.

analysis.originalLogic: Generic dominator computation tracked a postorder rank for every node during the DFS (`post_order_rank[...] = post_order_idx; post_order_idx += 1;`) and stored it in `Inner`. `Dominators::cmp_in_dominator_order` used this stored rank: for `Kind::General`, `g.post_order_rank[rhs].cmp(&g.post_order_rank[lhs])`; for `Kind::Path`, it used `lhs.index().cmp(&rhs.index())`. `CoverageGraph::cmp_in_dominator_order` delegated to that generic comparator.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: This is an optimization PR, not a confirmed bug fix. The historical transformation was the pre-PR implementation: it collected postorder rank during every generic dominator computation even though the source says the mapping was "used exclusively for `cmp_in_dominator_order` on the final product." The replacement moves that obligation into `InstrumentCoverage`: generic dominators no longer compute or store postorder rank, and `CoverageGraph` builds `dominator_order_rank` from a second reverse-postorder traversal, then compares `self.dominator_order_rank[a].cmp(&self.dominator_order_rank[b])`. No semantic error is claimed for the old code; it was correct but did extra work for non-coverage dominator users.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust compiler dominance/coverage graphs whose nodes are `BasicCoverageBlock`s and whose start node is reachable from the graph entry. The PR explicitly asserts reachability for the coverage graph: `assert_eq!(reverse_post_order.len(), this.num_nodes());` with the comment "The coverage graph is created by traversal, so all nodes are reachable." The comparator is a deterministic total ordering, not a dominance predicate: if `a` dominates `b`, then `a < b`; unrelated nodes may be ordered arbitrarily but consistently.
analysis.summary: InstrumentCoverage optimization: remove dominator-order bookkeeping from the generic dominator implementation and compute a coverage-local reverse-postorder rank only when CoverageGraph needs a dominator-compatible total order. The ranking invariant must remain: if `a` dominates `b`, then `rank[a] < rank[b]`.
analysis.trigger: Generic graph dominators are computed for callers that do not need dominator-order information, while coverage graph comparisons still need an ordering where dominators precede dominated nodes. The PR trigger is visible in: "Dominator-order information is only needed for coverage graphs, and is easy enough to collect by just traversing the graph again."
preconditions: The coverage graph must be traversable from `this.start_node()` with all nodes reachable; otherwise the reverse-postorder length assertion fails or unvisited nodes retain the default rank 0.
The rank must be assigned from `graph::iterate::reverse_post_order`, with ascending rank order, so that a dominator receives a smaller rank than its dominated node.
Only `CoverageGraph` should depend on the specialized rank after the optimization; generic `Dominators` no longer exposes `cmp_in_dominator_order`.
The comparator must preserve the historical contract for both old `Kind::Path` and `Kind::General` cases: it orders nodes for deterministic traversal and cannot be used to decide dominance by itself.
Exact ordering of unrelated nodes is not semantically required; only consistency and the dominator-before-dominated implication are required.
pitfalls: Using preorder rank or plain node-index order without confirming the dominator-before-dominated invariant can violate the comparator contract.

Storing the old postorder rank but comparing it in the wrong direction is a trap: the old code compared `post_order_rank[rhs].cmp(&post_order_rank[lhs])`, which is equivalent to ascending reverse-postorder order.
Removing the generic `cmp_in_dominator_order` without initializing `dominator_order_rank` in CoverageGraph leaves default ranks and breaks coverage ordering.
Unreachable nodes would retain the zero-initialized rank; the coverage-specific assertion documents that this input case is excluded.
An exact-order differential test is too strong for unrelated nodes because the source explicitly says their relative order is arbitrary but consistent.

The `Kind::Path` shortcut previously used node indices, while the new coverage rank uses reverse postorder; tests should verify the ordering invariant rather than assume identical implementation details.
analysis.testStrategy: Add focused compiler coverage tests that exercise graphs with straight-line paths, diamonds, loops, and multiple blocks. For each generated/reachable CoverageGraph, check comparator consistency (antisymmetry/transitivity) and, for every pair for which `dominates(a, b)` is true, assert `rank[a] < rank[b]`. Where the old generic comparator remains available in a test harness, differentially compare old `cmp_in_dominator_order` against the new rank comparator over all reachable coverage-graph node pairs, allowing differences only for unrelated nodes. Run existing coverage/MIR regression tests to confirm that moving rank collection does not change emitted coverage mappings or pass output. Do not assume tests were executed here; the supplied patch contains no regression-test changes.
evidence: Dominator-order information is only needed for coverage graphs, and is easy enough to collect by just traversing the graph again.
This avoids wasted work when computing graph dominators for any other purpose.
Postorder mapping (used exclusively for `cmp_in_dominator_order` on the final product)
// compute the post order index (rank) for each node
/// Allows nodes to be compared in some total order such that _if_
/// `a` dominates `b`, then `a < b`. If neither node dominates the other,
/// their relative order is consistent but arbitrary.
// The dominator rank of each node is just its index in a reverse-postorder traversal.
// The coverage graph is created by traversal, so all nodes are reachable.
Provide deterministic ordering of nodes such that, if any two nodes have a dominator
relationship, the dominator will always precede the dominated. (The relative ordering
of two unrelated nodes will also be consistent, but otherwise the order has no
meaning.) This method cannot be used to determine if either Node dominates the other.
